verdicts.reason: The Double Enclosure: the human-authorship requirement as settled by the Thaler litigation (cert. denied 2 March 2026), the question the courts did not reach, the archive's reading of the doctrine as a double enclosure, its forecast of concealment, the training-side litigation as a parallel track and the Compositional Authorship Standard. The archive's categories (enclosure, the confession protocol, compositional judgment) applied to the law on who or what can be an author, the census's class for the entity.

EA-HETERONYMY-01, the census's anchor, at §0 and §1: legal accountability held apart from exhaustive authorial identity; the civil name as the atomic unit of attribution, to which copyright attaches. The archive's category of the civil-name attribution regime applied to the law of authorship (the class). Its other string candidates (§1 on attribution regimes; §3) restate the same lineage and add nothing at this locus.

Provenance Is What Authorship Must Endure, §3 Position 2: the archive's taxonomy applied to copyright law's position on AI-assisted works, with the limit it states (no process evidence). #1369 is a later version of the same packet (the same sentence, line 120): grouped with #729 as one lineage (S4), its instances kept in the provenance graph.

Adversarial by Origin (hop from #195): copyright litigation over training 'grinds on years behind the taking' (§I) and uncycled law, formalized without a litigated case, 'maximally broad' (§VII). The archive's category of law without jurisprudence applied to litigation involving AI, the record object the census and the field give for the entity (class 1).

r.30 THE RUBY MOOT (hop from #195): the archive's court of record, whose matters in dispute are authorship, names, classifications, erasures and the resolution of entities, and whose power is the record; it receives from #194 that the law of machine meaning is formalized without jurisprudence. The archive's own record of authorship disputes, applied to the class.

Docket No. 1, Mary Lee Sharks v. The Composition Layer (hop from #195): an authorship dispute with the composition layer, pleaded in the alternative. The archive's court applied to an authorship dispute involving AI (class 2).
